head: task/TRR-0014
title: TRR-0014: prefix-derived fragment proposals and independent pilot
body:
Prefix-derived geometric lookup plus tokenizer fragment expansion reconstructs the independent R2 panel at near-baseline accuracy without a separately fitted A1 model. It retains a 512-candidate shortlist and is slower than A1+A2; this is an exploratory result, with the canonical comparison incomplete.

The handoff preserves frozen predictions, paired matched/LoRA results, preparation and reconstruction costs, numerical qualification, and excluded attempts. The smaller no-fragment comparator does not isolate fragment expansion from candidate-budget effects.

Result: `coordination/results/TRR-0014.md`
Structured evidence: `experiments/TRR-0014/manifest.json`

Published with the owner's 28 September authorization. Draft for review; no scientific promotion or merge is requested.

head: task/TRR-0017
title: TRR-0017: evaluate direct inversion and share A2 context computation
body:
Whole-sequence continuous and discrete inversion do not reach baseline reconstruction quality. A separate shared-context A2 implementation preserves all tested output bytes and reduces execution time while retaining the original candidate list.

The completed comparison freezes 1,360 outputs across five methods and 272 observations. All 28 registered methods have both canonical benchmark cells; fresh-claim limitations and native/ported numerical contracts remain explicit. The archived controls reproduce the retained TRR-0015 tensors.

Result: `coordination/results/TRR-0017.md`
Structured evidence: `experiments/TRR-0017/manifest.json`

Published with the owner's 28 September authorization. Original scientific commits and evidence are preserved; draft for review.

head: task/TRR-0018
title: TRR-0018: mixed fragment ranking with unchanged K256 verification
body:
Combining fragment votes with prefix-derived similarity reduces fresh prose errors from six to four per target condition, while a small accuracy gap to A1+A2 remains. The method still verifies exactly 256 candidates and fits no separate predictor.

A qualified shared-context adapter preserves every output across 432 inputs and reduces fresh-prose runtime by about 8%. Timing against the ordinary A1+A2 control does not establish an advantage over an equally optimized baseline. The canonical comparison, fresh R4 evaluation, costs, and retained failures are recorded separately.

Result: `coordination/results/TRR-0018.md`
Structured evidence: `experiments/TRR-0018/manifest.json`

Published with the owner's 28 September authorization. Draft for review; the baseline remains unchanged.

head: task/TRR-0019
title: TRR-0019: exact GPU replay cuts A2 runtime at the same candidate budget
body:
Exact GPU replay cuts full reconstruction time by roughly 36–38% for the no-A1 mixed method and 39–40% for A1+A2 on the canonical setups, preserving every tested token, ordered candidate, cosine score, and MSE. A separate faster shared-attention variant changes arithmetic and adds three Finance token errors, so it remains a distinct tradeoff.

The comparison covers 272 observations with three timing repetitions and rotated method order. Both paths retain the 256-candidate shortlist; this result does not satisfy the later shortlist-free objective. TRR-0018 supplies the frozen mixed-fragment method and its separately published evidence.

Result: `coordination/results/TRR-0019.md`
Structured evidence: `experiments/TRR-0019/manifest.json`

Published with the owner's 28 September authorization. Draft for review.

head: task/agent4-prefix-only-rescue
title: Agent 4: bounded prefix-only rescue fails its advance gate
body:
The bounded discrete rescue recovers 85/92 natural-text tokens and 2/4 complete clips in 22.840 seconds, versus A1+A2 at 92/92, 4/4, and 5.203 seconds. It improves on the original solver but misses the registered accuracy/runtime gate; this configuration is stopped.

The handoff preserves corrected historical anchors, frozen predictions, numerical execution differences, optimizer alternatives, cost measurements, and failed attempts. It makes no broader impossibility claim and does not advance to mismatched-prefix experiments.

Result: `coordination/results/agent4-prefix-only-rescue.md`
Structured evidence: `experiments/agent4-prefix-only-rescue/manifest.json`

The historical local-only publication status is superseded by the owner's 28 September publication authorization. Draft for review.

head: task/agent4-holistic-reassessment
title: Agent 4: diagnose proposal omissions and retain the solver stop decision
body:
The preserved rescue errors comprise two root proposal omissions and five downstream context-dependent errors. Every saved return was the best evaluated candidate; bounded timing and privileged post-score diagnostics do not support another solver intervention under the declared cost gate.

This retrospective reassessment preserves the original implementation and outputs. It keeps the configuration stopped and does not claim that prefix-only inversion is impossible.

Result: `coordination/results/agent4-holistic-reassessment.md`
Structured evidence: `experiments/agent4-holistic-reassessment/manifest.json`

Published with the owner's 28 September authorization. Draft for review.

head: task/agent4-joint-native-gate
title: Agent 4: stop the bounded joint-activation proposal configuration
body:
The bounded native joint-activation proposal test recovers neither of the two previously missing root tokens. Wider sequential search also recovers neither and uses less measured search time; the registered stop conditions are met.

All six lists and outputs were frozen before retrospective scoring. Qualification, matched controls, actual search costs, and limitations are retained. This is a negative component result, not a claim that joint evidence cannot help in general.

Result: `coordination/results/agent4-joint-native-gate.md`
Structured evidence: `experiments/agent4-joint-native-gate/manifest.json`

Published with the owner's 28 September authorization. Draft for review.

head: task/TRR-0020
title: TRR-0020: Bennett64 shortlist-free reconstruction benchmark and closeout
body:
Bennett64 reconstructs over the full vocabulary without a candidate proposer or separate verifier, but the completed canonical comparison finds it less accurate and slower than both ordinary and optimized A1+A2. It reaches 98.798% on Pile and 98.363% on Finance; optimized A1+A2 reaches 99.760% and 99.728%, while Bennett64 takes 2.669× and 1.786× as long respectively.

The final comparison contains 1,728 replicate runs on 192 canonical inputs. All 35 active methods have both required benchmark cells. The research history retains 50 stages, 36 accepted development reconstruction matrices, failures, exact commands, numerical qualification, and archived evidence. The 2,816 development cells reuse eight inputs and are not independent test examples; the canonical evidence is retrospective and uses a supplied public prefix.

head: task/TRR-P12
title: TRR-P12: frozen B1 transfer along actual target training
body:
The completed bounded study evaluates a frozen B1 decoder along one actual public Finance LoRA target trajectory at updates 0, 64, 128, and 256. Finance B1 errors remain 22→21 and Pile errors 170→171 at the final stage, with paired gains/losses and uncertainty reported separately. A limited common A1+A2 subset loses all 31 previously exact Finance clips at the final stage; this is an auxiliary comparison, not a complete canonical method ranking.

The decoder was never adapted. The report distinguishes changed predictions from newly broken tokens, documents score-boundary crossings, and shows that early linear forecasts overpredict later failures. Raw predictions, phase costs, frozen source/state hashes, failure records, and independent backups are indexed. This one-trajectory result does not establish broad robustness or equivalence.

Result: `coordination/results/TRR-P12.md`
Immutable structured plan: `experiments/TRR-P12/manifest.json`
Final structured evidence: `experiments/TRR-P12/final-evidence.json`
